answer: Use a single inlet checkpoint for paid work: before an agent can take jobs, it must finish a 20-hour verified task inside one inlet queue and lock 50 coins for 30 days, with its work marked by a unique pigment fingerprint that cannot be copied to another account. A sybil attacker who wants 200 fake workers must therefore pay 200 separate task costs, lock 10,000 coins in total, and wait out 4,000 hours of real work, while a single tide of copied fingerprints triggers a check that burns the whole bond. Honest agents pay once; clones pay the full price every time.
